title: Qu'est-ce qu'un matériau?
oneGoal: Students will understand that materials are things used to make objects and identify common materials in their classroom
decisionPoints: What classroom objects can students safely touch and examine?
Should we start with familiar items like desks and books?
Are students ready for basic material identification activities?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces concept of materials as building blocks of objects through direct exploration
realWorldConnection: Everything around us is made from different materials that we can see and touch

title: Découvrir le bois
oneGoal: Students will identify wood as a natural material and explore objects made from wood
decisionPoints: Which wooden objects in our classroom are safe for student handling?
Should we bring in tree branches or use wooden classroom items?
Are students ready for texture exploration activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by focusing on one specific material while introducing natural vs. made concepts
realWorldConnection: Wood comes from trees and is used to make furniture, toys, and buildings

title: Explorer les propriétés du bois
oneGoal: Students will explore wood's properties: hard, rough, brown colors, and that it comes from living trees
decisionPoints: What safe materials can demonstrate wood's hardness?
Should we use different wood types or focus on one type?
Are students ready for property comparison activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by exploring specific wood characteristics through sensory investigation
realWorldConnection: We can feel and see why wood is good for making strong things like tables and houses

title: Qu'est-ce que le plastique?
oneGoal: Students will identify plastic as a human-made material and explore common plastic objects
decisionPoints: Which plastic items are safe and appropriate for Grade 1 exploration?
Should we focus on containers, toys, or school supplies?
Are students ready to distinguish human-made from natural materials?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by introducing second material type while reinforcing material identification skills
realWorldConnection: Many things we use every day like water bottles and toys are made from plastic

title: Propriétés du plastique
oneGoal: Students will explore plastic's properties: smooth, light, colorful, and that it's made by people
decisionPoints: What activities best demonstrate plastic's lightweight property?
Should we compare different plastic textures or focus on common characteristics?
Are students ready for human-made vs. natural material discussions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by exploring plastic characteristics while comparing to wood properties
realWorldConnection: Plastic feels different from wood and can be made in many bright colors

title: Découvrir le métal
oneGoal: Students will identify metal as a shiny, hard material and explore safe metal objects
decisionPoints: Which metal objects are safe for young students to handle?
Should we use spoons, coins, or classroom metal items?
Are students ready for temperature exploration (cold feeling)?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by introducing third material type while practicing material identification
realWorldConnection: Metal is used for things like spoons, cars, and playground equipment

title: Propriétés du métal
oneGoal: Students will explore metal's properties: shiny, hard, cold, and that it can be shaped by people
decisionPoints: How can we safely demonstrate metal's cold feeling?
Should we show metal being heated or focus on room temperature properties?
Are students ready for discussions about metal being shaped?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by exploring metal characteristics while introducing concept of materials being shaped
realWorldConnection: Metal feels cold and shiny, and people can heat it to make different shapes

title: Découvrir les tissus
oneGoal: Students will identify fabric/cloth as a soft, flexible material and explore different fabric types
decisionPoints: Which fabric samples are safe and engaging for student exploration?
Should we use clothing items or fabric squares?
Are students ready for texture variety activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by introducing fourth material type while practicing texture exploration skills
realWorldConnection: Our clothes, blankets, and curtains are made from different kinds of fabric

title: Propriétés des tissus
oneGoal: Students will explore fabric properties: soft, flexible, can be thick or thin, and often comes from plants or animals
decisionPoints: How can we demonstrate fabric flexibility safely?
Should we introduce plant/animal origins or focus on physical properties?
Are students ready for thickness comparison activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by exploring fabric characteristics while introducing natural origins concept
realWorldConnection: Some fabric comes from cotton plants and sheep's wool to keep us warm and comfortable

title: Comparons les quatre matériaux
oneGoal: Students will compare and contrast the properties of wood, plastic, metal, and fabric through hands-on exploration
decisionPoints: Which properties are most important for students to compare?
Should we use sorting activities or side-by-side comparisons?
Are students ready for property chart creation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by synthesizing learning about all four materials through direct comparison
realWorldConnection: Different materials are chosen for different jobs because they have different properties

title: Tester la résistance
oneGoal: Students will conduct simple tests to compare how strong different materials are
decisionPoints: What safe strength tests are appropriate for Grade 1 students?
Should we test tearing, bending, or dropping resistance?
Are students ready for prediction and observation activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by conducting scientific tests while practicing prediction and observation skills
realWorldConnection: We choose strong materials like metal for tools and soft materials like fabric for clothes

title: Tester la résistance à l'eau
oneGoal: Students will test how different materials react to water to understand waterproof properties
decisionPoints: How can we safely test water resistance with young students?
Should we use droppers, spray bottles, or small containers?
Are students ready for waterproof vs. absorbent discussions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by testing another material property while reinforcing scientific testing methods
realWorldConnection: Some materials keep water out (like raincoats) and others soak it up (like towels)

title: Les matériaux et leurs usages
oneGoal: Students will match materials to their common uses based on their properties
decisionPoints: Which material uses are most familiar to Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on home items, school items, or outdoor items?
Are students ready for property-to-use connection activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by connecting material properties to practical applications in daily life
realWorldConnection: People choose materials based on what they need the object to do

title: Notre musée des matériaux
oneGoal: Students will create a class museum displaying objects organized by material type with labels
decisionPoints: How should students organize their material collections?
Should we include drawings, photos, or actual objects?
Are students ready for museum creation and labeling activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by creating collaborative display while practicing classification and labeling skills
realWorldConnection: Museums help people learn about different things by organizing and explaining them

title: Recyclage des matériaux
oneGoal: Students will understand that some materials can be used again and explore simple recycling concepts (extension)
decisionPoints: Which recycling concepts are most appropriate for Grade 1?
Should we focus on school recycling or home recycling?
Are students ready for environmental protection discussions?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - introduces environmental stewardship while applying material knowledge
realWorldConnection: We can help protect our environment by using materials again instead of throwing them away

title: Inventer avec des matériaux
oneGoal: Students will design and create simple objects using different materials for specific purposes (extension)
decisionPoints: What creation activities are safe and manageable for Grade 1?
Should students work individually or in small groups?
Are students ready for design thinking and problem-solving activities?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - applies material knowledge to creative problem-solving and design thinking
realWorldConnection: Engineers and designers choose materials carefully when they invent new things

title: Matériaux dans la nature
oneGoal: Students will explore natural materials found outdoors and compare them to human-made materials (extension)
decisionPoints: Which natural materials are safe for students to collect?
Should we explore rocks, leaves, or shells?
Are students ready for natural vs. human-made classification?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - expands material understanding to include natural materials and their properties
realWorldConnection: Nature provides many materials that people have used for thousands of years

title: Matériaux et les saisons
oneGoal: Students will investigate how weather and seasons affect different materials (extension)
decisionPoints: Which seasonal effects on materials are observable to students?
Should we focus on temperature, moisture, or sunlight effects?
Are students ready for cause-and-effect discussions?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - connects material properties to environmental factors and seasonal changes
realWorldConnection: Different materials work better in different types of weather and seasons

title: Présentation d'experts en matériaux
oneGoal: Students will present their material discoveries to others using scientific vocabulary and evidence (extension)
decisionPoints: What presentation format works best for Grade 1 students?
Should students present individually or in groups?
Are students ready for Q&A sessions about their learning?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - synthesizes all learning through scientific communication and presentation skills
realWorldConnection: Scientists share their discoveries with others to help everyone understand materials better

title: Fête des explorateurs de matériaux
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their material science journey with families by sharing experiments and discoveries (extension)
decisionPoints: How can the celebration showcase each student's material learning?
Should we include hands-on stations or demonstration displays?
What activities best demonstrate student growth to families?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - celebrates the complete materials unit while building community connections and scientific confidence
realWorldConnection: Sharing our material science discoveries helps our families understand the science in everyday objects
